findings.heading: Convert to factor / Faktöre dönüştürme
findings.proposition: The whole paragraph explaining that the unique values are now factor levels, that the level order can be printed with base R levels() or viewed with table()/tabyl(), that the default order is alpha-numeric, and that NA is not a factor level, is untranslated: line 113 of the Turkish file is the English source text verbatim.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish-only reader cannot read the paragraph and misses four facts, most importantly that NA is not a factor level and that levels() prints the order. They then cannot interpret the levels() output in the chunk that immediately follows.

findings.heading: Convert to factor / Faktöre dönüştürme
findings.proposition: The English says the PLOT order now makes intuitive sense; the Turkish says the order in the TABLE ('tablodaki sırası') now makes intuitive sense, while the chunk immediately beside it is a ggplot geom_bar bar chart and contains no table call.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader looks for a table output that the chunk never produces, and misses that the point being demonstrated is the effect of fct_relevel() on the x-axis ordering of a plot.

findings.heading: By summary statistic of another column / Başka bir sütunun özet istatistiğine göre
findings.proposition: The English names the literal string arguments passed to fct_reorder() as "median", and the alternatives "max", "mean", "min"; the Turkish renders them as the code-formatted Turkish words `medyan`, `maks`, `ortalama`, `min`, which are not valid R function names and do not match the chunk beside it, which uses fct_reorder(delay_cat, ct_blood, "median").
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader who copies the prose and writes fct_reorder(delay_cat, ct_blood, "medyan") or "ortalama" gets an error, because R has no function of that name.

findings.heading: By "end" value / "Son" değere göre
findings.proposition: The English says fct_reorder2() orders the levels and therefore the LEGEND to align with the vertical order of the lines at the end of the plot; the Turkish says it aligns the levels and therefore the TITLE ('*başlığın*'), naming a different plot element.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader is told the plot title is reordered, which is impossible, and misses the actual benefit of fct_reorder2(): the legend entries line up with the line order at the right-hand edge of the plot. The following paragraph then uses 'açıklama' (legend) for the same idea, so the two paragraphs contradict each other.

findings.heading: Show all levels / Tüm seviyeleri gösterme
findings.proposition: The English gives the motivating example as preparing many figures for MULTIPLE JURISDICTIONS; the Turkish replaces it with a tautology, 'many analyses (e.g. for more than one analysis)', so the jurisdictions example is absent.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader loses the concrete epidemiological reason for standardising levels: producing the same figure for several districts or regions whose data differ. The remaining parenthetical explains nothing.

findings.heading: Show all levels / Tüm seviyeleri gösterme
findings.proposition: The English says legends and tables should look identical even with varying levels of DATA COMPLETION or data composition; the Turkish keeps only data composition ('veri kompozisyonu') and drops data completion.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader misses one of the two situations that make fixed factor levels necessary: a dataset that is only partly reported, where a level exists but has no rows yet.

findings.heading: Epiweeks in the data / Verilerde epiweeks
findings.proposition: The English states the conversion of the epiweek column to the display format happens *within the data frame itself*, italicised as the contrast with the preceding 'in a plot' approach; the Turkish drops that clause entirely.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader loses the distinction this whole section rests on, that option 1 changes the stored column rather than only the plot display, and may assume the change is again plot-local.

findings.heading: Convert to factor / Faktöre dönüştürme
findings.proposition: The English says the level order is supplied AS a character vector TO the `levels = ` argument of factor(); the Turkish inverts the relation and says the order is set 'according to the `levels = ` argument in the character vector' ('karakter vektöründeki `levels =` argümanına göre').
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader is left without the actual calling syntax for base R factor(), and may look for a levels= argument inside a vector rather than passing a vector to levels=.

findings.heading: Factors / Faktörler (intro)
findings.proposition: The English says plot legends fluctuate when CERTAIN VALUES are temporarily absent from the data; the Turkish generalises this to the data itself being temporarily absent ('verilerin geçici olarak yok olması'), dropping the point that it is individual values that go missing.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader does not learn the specific failure this chapter exists to prevent, that a category with zero rows silently disappears from a legend, and may read it as a statement about missing data sets.
